children: Pinnacle Financial Partners reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $1.31B and net income available to common shareholders of $364M, with diluted EPS of $2.4. Results were higher than a year earlier, primarily reflecting the January merger with Synovus.
Revenue was $1.31B, compared with $544M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 141%.
Net income available to common shareholders was $364M, compared with $169M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 116%.
Diluted EPS was $2.40, compared with $2.19 in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 10%.
The January 2026 Synovus merger expanded the company’s footprint to 382 branches and 501 ATMs across the Southeast.

Third-quarter net interest income rose 148% and non-interest revenue increased 122% year over year, primarily reflecting the combined operations. Core banking fees, wealth management, capital markets and BHG loan production also contributed to business momentum.
Loans reached $89.8B, with growth outside merger effects balanced across specialty and geographic business units.
For 2026, management expects loan growth of 9% to 11%, deposit growth of 8% to 10% and adjusted revenue of $5.0B to $5.2B, assuming stable interest rates and economic conditions.
